Novel listing/search archetype; represents browsing, filtering and discovery.
User-published novel detail archetype and route into reading.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains the same white, light-only surface as the default capture; no dark-theme rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme/light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text and controls.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the hero .slick-track moved from matrix x=-1900 to x=-3198.39 in 4.5 seconds and retained a 1s transform transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable autoplay and remove or greatly shorten non-essential carousel transitions under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-contrast / forced-colors: controls, text and scrollbars remain visible under high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: axe-core found serious color-contrast failures on ranking labels and the consent interface, with 56 additional nodes requiring review.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe semantic tokens and verify normal, high-contrast and forced-colors states.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero view-transition rules; page changes are traditional abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation and reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: Long listing/detail pages retain static dense chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state/container handling or progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome sparingly and add declarative scroll-state/progress affordances on long reading/list pages.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: Every fresh-path mobile capture is obscured by a centered consent interstitial before the requested content can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface with equally visible accept/reject choices and persistent preference access.

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports zero dialog/popover/details primitives while the consent UI adds multiple H1s and a custom overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with <dialog> and transient UI with popover, preserving focus, escape and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: Mobile captures devote large portions of the page to stacked promotional sidebars, banners and navigation around much smaller primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary promotions on narrow screens and prioritize the selected work, episode list or form.

findings.summary: Layout adapts to narrow viewports with no horizontal overflow and no fixed pixel widths forcing a desktop layout on mobile; viewport meta present; fluid scaling and intrinsic sizing rather than brittle breakpoints.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360px viewport, Chrome lays out a 1000-1002px desktop canvas and scales it to about 0.36; text and controls are tiny rather than reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and fluid responsive layouts that render at a true 360 CSS px width.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero @container rules, and the same multi-column desktop components are merely scaled down across all mobile captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, sidebars and navigation containment and adapt them with container queries.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: The target probe found 127 of 880 visible controls smaller than 24px; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets with adequate spacing, non-hover equivalents and clear :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The representative primary flow can be completed end-to-end with predictable steps, no avoidable dead ends, no hidden required information, and no needless detours through modals, account walls, or upsells.
findings.evidence: The registration and content paths are immediately interrupted by consent, while scaled desktop forms make the primary journey difficult on a common mobile viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users reach and complete browse/read/register journeys without a blocking interstitial and with mobile-first form steps.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: After an empty registration submit, required controls became :invalid but no role=alert/error content appeared and focus was not moved to the first error.
findings.suggestedFix: Show an error summary, announce it with aria-live/role=alert, set field errors after interaction and focus the first invalid field.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured performance 0.42 on home and 0.37 on novel detail; home CLS was 0.509 and novel-detail LCP was 17.0s with 840ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reserve layout space, remove blocking work and retest LCP/CLS/INP on representative templates.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive observed home CLS 0.670, including one shift of 0.557; 20 images lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/banner slots with dimensions or aspect-ratio and stabilize carousel/ad insertion.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 5.8s main-thread work and 1.7s JavaScript execution on home, with TBT 488ms; detail/register TBT exceeded 840ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks and defer or conditionally load non-essential widgets and analytics.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 201 requests and 13.45MB transferred; parser-inserted CSS/scripts are high-priority candidates and Lighthouse estimates 12.4MB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, defer parser-blocking scripts, add durable CDN caching and deliver only viewport-relevant images.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1.39MB unused JavaScript on novel detail; home loads 39 scripts and extensive third-party code.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage data to remove unused bundles, deduplicate libraries and load route/consent/analytics code conditionally.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: axe found unlabeled search, select and submit controls on every sampled page, 20 unnamed links on home, two untitled frames on novel detail, and unlabeled registration confirmation/captcha fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels/names, meaningful image-link alternatives and iframe titles; remove invalid/nested ARIA patterns.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: axe reported serious contrast failures on all three sampled templates, including primary buttons and consent text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to WCAG AA and test all component states.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: axe found content outside landmarks and duplicate/unnamed landmarks; the consent vendor markup injects several extra H1 headings into the document outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one content H1 per page, named landmarks, logical focus order and a trapped/restored modal focus cycle.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: The 1000px desktop layout is scaled to 360px, making body copy, navigation and form text visibly tiny in every mobile capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow at the device viewport with readable type sizes, line lengths and spacing instead of whole-page scaling.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Mobile uses a 1000px layout viewport and Lighthouse fails target-size; 127 controls are below 24px before considering 200% zoom.
findings.suggestedFix: Support 320px reflow/200% zoom and enlarge targets without disabling user scaling.

findings.summary: The page loads without console errors or uncaught exceptions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports browser console errors on home, novel detail and registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix first-party exceptions and failed integrations, and keep automated console-error checks in CI.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Although doctype/UTF-8 are valid, the image audit found 20 missing dimensions and Lighthouse found an incorrectly proportioned image on registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic image dimensions/aspect-ratio and correct distorted assets while retaining valid document metadata.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found deprecated APIs, missing large-script source maps and DevTools inspector issues on all sampled paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs, publish production source maps securely and clear browser Issues-panel warnings.

findings.summary: The page has a unique, descriptive <title> and a meta description.
findings.evidence: Home and content pages have descriptive metadata, but /register has an empty meta description and Lighthouse fails meta-description there.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique registration-page description and retain unique titles/descriptions per template.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors and the DOM has javascript:void(0) links; the viewport declaration produces a 1000px scaled layout on 360px devices.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and a correct responsive viewport plus genuine mobile reflow.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD despite representing an organization and many works; sampled entity pages expose no recorded structured-data evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Add validated Organization/WebSite and Book/CreativeWork metadata matching visible content, plus complete social cards.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP and HSTS are absent and all 19 observed cookies were flagged; 12 cookies lacked Secure and all used permissive SameSite=None except two.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and a nonce/hash CSP; minimize cookies and set Secure, HttpOnly and Lax/Strict according to purpose.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: Before consent, network capture reached 33 third-party origins and 11 known tracker domains; the consent text names 209 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential trackers until explicit consent, reduce vendors and events, and batch privacy-preserving analytics.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load, but the account flow offers password registration only; no passkey/WebAuthn capability was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/authentication and retain passwords only as a well-protected recovery fallback.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer and least-privilege permissions policies, then layer Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang=ja is correct, but the CSS probe found only six logical-property rules and the fixed physical desktop layout does not adapt even to a narrower same-language viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep lang=ja, set direction explicitly where needed and migrate layout spacing/sizing to logical properties with writing-mode tests.

findings.summary: No deceptive design: no confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised ads, or nagging consent walls; honest defaults; clear pricing and consent; easy reversal/cancel; predictable, declaratively-wired actions; and no hidden-text tricks (hidden content stays deep-linkable and indexable rather than used to deceive).
findings.evidence: A blocking consent dialog offers prominent Consent and Manage options but no equally direct Reject action, while tracker requests are already active before a choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide symmetric accept/reject controls and prevent optional processing until an affirmative choice.

findings.summary: Forms prevent and recover from mistakes humanely: validate after interaction (not prematurely), give clear required-field feedback, announce errors accessibly, and signal invalid fields visibly rather than blaming the user.
findings.evidence: Empty registration submission produced native invalid states but no page error summary, accessible announcement or focus movement.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, identify fields in plain language, announce a summary and move focus predictably.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: Registration username, email, password and confirmation fields all expose empty autocomplete values; axe also finds confirmation/captcha unlabeled.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply username, email, new-password and appropriate one-time-code tokens and label every field.

findings.summary: Checkout, subscription, consent, authentication and account-management flows are clear, reversible, and proportionate: pricing and commitments are visible, cancellation is findable, sensitive actions re-authenticate when appropriate, and users are not tricked into continuity.
findings.evidence: The sampled account flow relies on password-only registration and is obscured by consent; no passkey capability or clear privacy-preserving default is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Make consent optional and reversible, add passkeys, and clearly explain account commitments and recovery before submission.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: The homepage transfers 11.86MB of images; 48 images use legacy formats, 10 are oversized, 22 lack srcset and 21 below-fold images are not lazy.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes and lazy-load below-fold media while prioritizing only LCP.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: The homepage makes 201 requests, loads 39 scripts and sends traffic to 33 third-party origins, including multiple analytics systems before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors, defer background fetches and stop analytics/media work when hidden or unconsented.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 150 requests and 12.91MB; home imagery alone reaches 11.86MB and individual covers exceed 600KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template budgets for total bytes/requests/third parties and enforce them in CI, with consent-gated loading.

taskList.title: Build a genuine responsive mobile layout and accessible component system
Gate and minimize tracking; deploy complete browser security policies
Cut image/network weight and stabilize the critical rendering path
Replace the blocking asymmetric consent interstitial
Repair names, labels, landmarks, contrast and focus/error handling
Clear console/deprecation/asset issues and improve metadata
